display.purpose: Page headline only — Archivo 800, two lines, second line muted.

numeral.purpose: Every read number: timers, cells, scores, counts — Geist Mono tabular.

label.purpose: Printed micro-type: field keys, plate captions, footers — 10px caps, tracked.

shadows.name: sheet-setdown
shadows.purpose: One soft ambient set-down shadow under a signature bordered sheet (light only; dark uses borders).

shadows.name: ink-press
shadows.purpose: Soft downward press under the primary ink button.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: The single easing curve for every entrance and state change.

motion.name: cell-fill-cadence
motion.purpose: The answer grid's staggered fill — the page's one authored moment.

motion.name: rule-draw
motion.purpose: Hairline rules draw in as sections and ruled entries enter view.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: framer MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"; decorative loops gated off, transforms snap
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion the sheet renders complete: no loops, no pulses, states resolve instantly.

narrative.overview: Real IELTS's student-facing surfaces behave like the document a candidate fills under time pressure: a cool paper-white ground, engraving-ink text, fine hairline rules, and numbered cells arranged in quiet grids. One indigo ink does all the pointing and filling — the same role a ballpoint plays on a paper answer sheet. Nothing floats, nothing glows, nothing shouts; the page's authority comes from exam-document discipline, not from landing-page decoration. The world is deliberately flat: depth comes from hairlines, boxed fields, and rare soft ambient shadows under signature sheets. Dark mode is the same exam hall at night: zinc-950 ground, indigo-400 ink, unchanged discipline.
keyCharacteristics: Ruled-sheet structure: full-width hairlines separate every section; content lives in bordered, boxed fields — never in floating rounded cards.
One ink (indigo-700 light / indigo-400 dark); emerald and red appear only as correct/wrong semantics.
Geist Mono tabular numerals wherever a number is read (timers, question numbers, scores, counts).
Archivo extrabold display voice with a muted second line; Inter body at a 65ch measure.
Drafting annotations: micro-caps numeric callouts pinned to the interface with hairline leaders, real numbers only.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Indigo is the only color that fills. Emerald and red are marking, not decoration; no other hue appears, and the ink never becomes a gradient.

rules.name: The Fine Rule Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn with 1px hairlines (#e4e4e7 light / #27272a dark), never with nested cards, side stripes, or shadow boxes. If two things relate, they share a rule; if they don't, a rule separates them.

rules.name: The Real Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every numeral shown in demo or mockup content is a real quantity from the product (40 questions, 21 books, band scale); demonstration data is labeled by its plate header, never presented as a claim.

rules.name: The Carried Weight Rule
rules.body: Headings carry their own weight — no kicker or eyebrow sits above any heading, and emphasis comes from size and weight, never from gradient or color text.

rules.name: The Set-Down Rule
rules.body: A shadow means a sheet was set down on the desk: one soft, low-opacity, downward-blurred shadow under a bordered sheet. Never a colored halo, never a hard offset block, never on text.

dos: Do structure with hairlines (#e4e4e7 / #27272a) and boxed fields; sections separate by a full-width rule.
Do set every read number in Geist Mono with `tabular-nums`.
Do keep active/selected states as ink-filled or 2px ink-bordered cells — solid, confident marks.
Do theme browser surfaces from the palette: text selection (indigo at 14% light / 25% dark), focus outlines (ring tint), tabular numerals in data.

Do animate like a document being filled: one authored moment per surface (the answer grid filling), entrances as drawn rules or single reveals, exponential ease-out `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`, and instant states under reduced motion.
donts: Don't put a kicker or eyebrow above a heading; the heading carries its own weight.
Don't use gradient text, glass/blur decoration, icon tiles, or unicode glyphs as an icon system — icons are drawn (lucide), one stroke weight.
Don't use hard offset shadows, colored halos, or nested cards; a shadow is a set-down sheet, nothing else.
Don't number sections (01/02/03) — the four-step process is the only sequence, because the count is the content.
Don't tint the neutral grays or introduce a second accent hue; if a color isn't the ink or a marking state, it doesn't ship.
